title: Homogeneous coordinates preserve the normalized derived bar model and coefficient augmentation
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent profinite site, $G$ a profinite group with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$, and $N$ an internal $A$-module with trivial $G$-action [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $U$ for forgetting the action, $F=\Gamma_G$ for invariants and $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $s:N[0]\to I$, whose underlying resolution $Us$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put
$$T=\operatorname{Tot}_{p,q\geq0}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{p+1}],UI^q),\qquad V=\operatorname{Tot}_{p,q\geq0}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],UI^q).$$
Use the homogeneous action $(g\cdot f)(h_i)=g\cdot_{I^q}f(g^{-1}h_i)$ and alternating deletion differential for $T$, and the action-dependent inhomogeneous bar differential for $V$; both totals have vertical sign $(-1)^p$ [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions, def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sp-double-complex-total]. Let $\delta:I\to T$ be constants in bar degree zero. There is a cochain isomorphism $\chi:F(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ with slice formulas
$$\chi(f)(g_1,\ldots,g_p)=f(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_p),$$
$$\chi^{-1}(c)(h_0,\ldots,h_p)=h_0\cdot c(h_0^{-1}h_1,\ldots,h_{p-1}^{-1}h_p).$$
These formulas commute with both differentials and all profinite base changes, including $p=0$. Write $v=\chi F(\delta)$, the bar-zero inclusion of invariants. In the compatible model $\mathscr B_A(G;N)=QV$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar], the isomorphism $Q(\chi):QF(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B_A(G;N)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal M)$, and the normalized bar isomorphism is
$$\epsilon=Q(v)\circ u_I^{-1}\circ RF(Qs),$$
where $u_I$ is the canonical derived-unit isomorphism [def-sfb-right-derived-functor].

Put $R_N^p=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{p+1}],N)$ with diagonal argument action and deletion differential, and $U_N^p=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],N)$ with the trivial-action inhomogeneous differential. Postcomposition with $s^0$ into bidegree $(p,0)$ defines equivariant $t:R_N\to T$ and $j_{\rm chain}:U_N\to V$, representing the underived-to-derived map $j=Q(j_{\rm chain})$. These are cochain maps, and $t$ takes the constant augmentation of $N$ to $\delta s$. For every nonnegative equivariant complex $K$ and equivariant cochain map $e:K\to R_N$, let $\rho:F(K)\to U_N$ be prefix evaluation of $e$ by the displayed formula. Then
$$\chi\circ F(te)=j_{\rm chain}\circ\rho.$$
In degree $p$ the common component is $x\mapsto[(g_1,\ldots,g_p)\mapsto s^0(e^p(x)(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_p))]$ in $(p,0)$, and all other components vanish. No quasi-isomorphism assumption on $e$ or acyclicity assumption on the terms of $K$ or $R_N$ is made.

proof.text: Work on every slice over a profinite $S$, not just at global points. By [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data], an internal function is a natural family of evaluations on all $W\to S$. By [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] and [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions], being invariant means exactly $f(ah_0,\ldots,ah_p)=a f(h_0,\ldots,h_p)$ after every such base change. Consequently it is the equivariant internal Hom appearing in [lem-sfb-condensed-injective-bar-rows]: the free-generator adjunction sends $f$ to $[z]\otimes[h]\mapsto f|_z(h)$, with the parameter $z$ carrying trivial action. Conversely restrict an equivariant map to these generators. The two operations are inverse by the free adjunction. Apply that lemma to each injective $I^q$. Its formula gives $\chi_{p,q}^{-1}(c)(h)=h_0c(h_0^{-1}h_1,\ldots,h_{p-1}^{-1}h_p)$ and its inverse is evaluation at $(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_p)$. Indeed consecutive quotients telescope to $h_0^{-1}h_i$ and equivariance gives $h_0 f(1,h_0^{-1}h_1,\ldots,h_0^{-1}h_p)=f(h)$. This also verifies the formulas on every slice.

proof.text: The coface formulas in [lem-sfb-condensed-injective-bar-rows] identify alternating deletion with the action-dependent inhomogeneous differential. Explicitly, deletion of the first prefix gives $g_1c(g_2,\ldots,g_{p+1})$, deletion of prefix $i$ for $1\le i\le p$ replaces adjacent arguments by $g_ig_{i+1}$, and the last deletion drops $g_{p+1}$, with signs $(-1)^i$. In degree zero, $f(h)=h m$, so deletion gives $gm-m$. The lemma's naturality in equivariant maps of injectives, applied to $d_I^q$, gives vertical compatibility. All prefix and quotient maps commute with pullback of profinite parameters; this is also part of its base-change assertion.

proof.text: In each degree $n$, invariants commute with the finite diagonal sum: a tuple is fixed after every base change if and only if each of its finitely many components is fixed. The inclusions and projections therefore give $F(T)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}F(T^{p,q})$. Summing the slice isomorphisms of steps 1-2 yields $\chi$. The degreewise inverse is the sum of their inverses. Both preserve $p$ and hence commute with the sign $(-1)^p$ in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. They are inverse cochain maps. Negative degrees are zero, and the diagonal at zero has one summand. Constants in bar degree zero evaluate at $1$ to the same coefficient; thus $v=\chi F(\delta)$ is exactly the invariant inclusion into bar degree zero, with no extra sign.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] with $R=A$ and $J=G$. Both categories are Grothendieck abelian, $F$ has the normalized invariant adjunction, and its computation unit $u_I$ is invertible since $I$ is a nonnegative complex of injectives. Kernels commute with the condition of being fixed on every slice, so $F$ is left exact. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-injective-total-target], $U$ is exact and preserves injectives, and constants give the stated cochain map $\delta$. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-injective-bar-rows] separately to each equivariantly injective $I^q$: these are exactly the augmented horizontal rows of $V$. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-condensed-bar-total-augmentation] holds for $a=s$, with the stipulated underlying injective resolution $Us$. Its specified augmentation $b_I:F(I)\to V$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and its columns represent the entire derived internal Hom diagram on this same resolution. Step 3 identifies $v=b_I$, so $QV$ is the compatible model in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Write $u_{N[0]}$ for the derived unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Naturality says $RF(Qs)u_{N[0]}=u_I QF(s)$. Hence $u_I^{-1}RF(Qs)$ is the canonical resolution-computation comparison, with its normalization fixed by the actual unit, rather than just by cohomology. Composing with $Q(b_I)=Q(v)$ gives precisely $\epsilon=Q(v)u_I^{-1}RF(Qs)$. Finally localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] takes the cochain isomorphism and inverse of step 3 to inverse derived morphisms $Q(\chi)$ and $Q(\chi^{-1})$.

proof.text: Postcompose evaluations with $s^0$ to define $t$ and $j_{\rm chain}$ in $(p,0)$. The equivariance of $s$ means $s^0(gn)=g s^0(n)$ on every slice. Thus postcomposition respects the homogeneous action and the action face of the inhomogeneous differential; it respects the other faces by linearity. Also $d_I^0s^0=0$, since $s$ is a cochain map out of $N[0]$. The extra vertical component of either total differential is therefore zero, including its factor $(-1)^p$. These facts prove both cochain identities directly from [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data] and [def-sp-double-complex-total]. On a constant $n$, $t$ is the constant $s^0(n)$ in $(0,0)$, exactly $\delta s$; all other components of the augmentation vanish. For each $p$, put $H_p=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],-)$. By naturality of the derived unit in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], $\eta_{UI}QH_p(Us)=RH_p(QUs)\eta_{UN[0]}$. The canonical computation identifies $RH_p(QUN[0])$ with $QH_p(UI)$ by $\eta_{UI}^{-1}RH_p(QUs)$; consequently the underived-to-derived map becomes exactly $QH_p(Us)$ in this model. These are the postcomposition maps already constructed. They respect every face, so their compatible total is $j=Q(j_{\rm chain})$.

proof.text: For $x\in F(K^p)(S)$, equivariance of $e$ makes $e^p(x)$ invariant on every slice. Prefix evaluation defines $\rho^p(x)$ as an internal function by the natural evaluation-family description of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. It is linear and commutes with restrictions. Its cochain identity can be checked without an injectivity assumption on $N$: for an invariant homogeneous function $f$, the first deleted prefix is $g_1 f(1,g_2,g_2g_3,\ldots)$, each interior deletion multiplies the adjacent arguments, and the last drops the last argument. These are precisely the inhomogeneous faces. Since the action on $N$ is trivial the first coefficient action is the identity. In degree zero the difference is $n-n=0$. Combining this calculation with $e^{p+1}d_K=d_{R_N}e^p$ proves $\rho$ is a cochain map. No assertion that $R_N$ is acyclic has entered this calculation.

proof.text:
Evaluate the two composites on any slice and any $x\in F(K^p)$. In both cases the only nonzero total component is $(p,0)$ and its value is
$$ (g_1,\ldots,g_p)\longmapsto s^0\bigl(e^p(x)(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_p)\bigr). $$
This is evaluation followed by postcomposition on both sides; these commute by the internal-function specification [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Hence equality of the natural evaluation families gives $\chi F(te)=j_{\rm chain}\rho$. For $p=0$ the expression is $s^0(e^0(x)(1))$, so the same identity holds. Only equivariance and the cochain identities were used for $K,e$; neither a quasi-isomorphism of $e$ nor termwise acyclicity of $K$ or $R_N$ is required.
